ORIGIN_BACKFILL_RECONCILIATION.verdict: Legitimate. No new authorization boundary and no new deletion power: the mutation writes ONE enum field (Moment.origin) on rows it selected, deletes nothing, and is reachable only by an explicit operator act — the Home 'Provenance' panel's plan-then-confirm, or the headless twin `fanops origin-backfill --apply`. The daemon never reaches it. Read-only by default. `Ledger.snapshot` is taken BEFORE the transaction opens, so the whole write is one restore away, and the ordering is pinned by a test that restores the returned snapshot and asserts the labels are gone. Idempotent: an already-labelled row is counted, not rewritten. It refuses rather than adapts — the selection is licensed only while the day-selected lineage is strictly 1:1:1 with no cross-window post on a selected clip, all re-measured UNDER the lock, and a plan fingerprint the confirm must carry back means a ledger that moved between plan and confirm refuses instead of writing something the operator never saw. An AUTHORED origin (operator/machine) is never overwritten by the inference.

new_ledger_transaction_sites.why_legitimate: Short, no network, no LLM, no subprocess inside the lock. Bounded to the id-set the survey resolved and re-resolved under the lock; every STOP invariant is re-checked inside the transaction and a failure exits the block having written nothing. Guarded on both sides: `Ledger.snapshot(cfg)` immediately BEFORE gives the rollback, `write_audit` immediately AFTER gives the record — including on a refusal, so a refused attempt is as traceable as an applied one. Anchored by symbol, not line (STD-DOC-01).

MACHINE_REOPEN_ADMISSION_RECONCILIATION.verdict: Legitimate, and it REMOVES authorization power rather than adding it. The unit's whole point is that `adjust.amplify` re-opened a source by calling `request_moments` directly, walking past FANOPS_QUEUE_GATE — the only admission gate the system has. The guard now parks a machine-origin re-open on `Source.meta["pending_reopen"]` and writes nothing; this transaction is the OPERATOR's release of that park, reached only from a Studio POST (`/run/release-reopens`) and carrying the same live-backend confirm checkbox as its `release_batch` / `release_all_held` siblings. No network and no LLM inside the lock: `request_moments` writes an agent REQUEST file and flips the source state; the model round-trip happens on a later pass. Idempotent — a source with nothing parked is skipped, so a double-click releases 0 and re-parks nothing.

new_ledger_transaction_sites.what: pops each named source's `meta["pending_reopen"]` and replays the parked moment request through `request_moments(..., operator_release=True)`
new_ledger_transaction_sites.why_legitimate: Bounded to the explicit `source_ids` the operator submitted; touches one dict key per source plus the state flip `request_moments` already owns. The parked ORIGIN is replayed verbatim rather than relabelled `operator` — the release opens the guard with a key, not by destroying the provenance the park exists to record. Every failure degrades to `ActionResult(ok=False, ...)` with a `release_reopens_failed` breadcrumb, the shape `release_all_held` already uses; an uncaught raise rolls the transaction back to the prior save.

the_network_ambiguity_decision_table.note: This table is the system's best engineering. It is correct on both backends.

5xx.why: the request landed; the response failed

2xx with no recognisable id.why: it may be live; we cannot address it

401.why: every post will fail; never burn the queue (INV-11)

the_network_ambiguity_decision_table.the_load_bearing_consequence: poster.publish NEVER lets a transient escape. The ONLY exception that escapes is AuthError, re-raised first. THEREFORE _publish_one's outer retry loop can only ever re-run the media UPLOAD — never the publish POST. This asymmetry is the ENTIRE double-publish defence and it is CORRECT.
